desc: AFOSI is the Air Force's independent criminal investigative and counterintelligence field agency, established in 1948 on the FBI model, whose remit it states covers 'espionage, terrorism, crimes against property, violence against people, larceny, computer hacking, acquisition fraud, drug use and distribution, financial misdeeds, military desertion, corruption of the contracting process, and any other illegal activity that undermines the mission of the U.S. Air Force or the Department of Defense', with units 'located at most Air Force bases worldwide'. AFOSI matters to this board because it is the one component of the US government whose participation in a UFO disinformation campaign is documented from the government's own files and admitted by the officer who ran it. Between 1980 and 1983 AFOSI Special Agent Richard C. Doty, working out of the Kirtland Air Force Base detachment during the Manzano Weapons Storage Area intrusion investigations, fed fabricated documents about crash retrievals, alien liaison and a programme called AQUARIUS to the Albuquerque physicist Paul Bennewitz, who was conducting his own surveillance of the base perimeter; Bennewitz's mental collapse is the documented outcome. The AFOSI Kirtland file, released under FOIA and archived by NICAP, is the primary record; Doty's later personnel file, released in 321 pages by the New Mexico State Police under the state's Inspection of Public Records Act, is the corroborating one; and Doty has repeatedly acknowledged on the record that he passed disinformation under orders. The Bennewitz operation is the reason no claim in this field can be evaluated without asking who benefits from the claimant being believed. It also cuts the other way, and this is the part usually omitted: a counterintelligence agency does not build a bespoke disinformation apparatus around a private citizen with a telescope unless something at the perimeter of that installation was worth protecting. In September 2025 the Wall Street Journal reported an alleged Air Force practice codenamed YANKEE BLUE, in which personnel were said to have been shown fabricated material about recovered craft as a loyalty or security test; the Pentagon first denied that any such memo existed and then, in December 2025, reopened the search for it.

dossier.narrative:
Start with the charter, because it is unclassified and it is decisive. Air Force Mission Directive 39, signed 12 February 2024 by Lt. Gen. Stephen L. Davis as The Inspector General, states AFOSI's mission as identifying, exploiting, investigating, disrupting and neutralising criminal, terrorist and intelligence threats across all domains. Paragraph 3.3 designates AFOSI, by the Secretary of the Air Force, as the Department's counterintelligence component and its sole agency for counterintelligence investigations, collections, operations and analysis. Paragraph 3.2 gives it primary investigative authority over everything in its jurisdiction and provides that its investigations "will supersede any other DAF entity's investigation or inquiry." Paragraph 3.7 gives it counterintelligence responsibility for cleared contractor facilities under the National Industrial Security Program. Paragraph 3.8 gives it counterintelligence support to critical DoD research and development under DoDI-O 5240.24. Paragraph 3.16 gives it program security responsibility for all Department of the Air Force special access programs and for non-DAF SAPs where the DAF has been assigned responsibility, under AFPD 16-7 and AFI 16-701. And paragraph 2.2 requires the commander to notify the Secretary in writing of any instance in which a commander or any other Air Force official attempts to impede an investigation - an obligation that exists precisely because the situation arises.

Set that against the historical record published by AFOSI's own command historian, Dr. Deborah Kidwell, in August 2020. Her account states that at the inception of Project Sign, Air Force Materiel Command held responsibility for UFO reports, but that shortly after AFOSI's creation in 1948 it took over that responsibility under the name Project Grudge. Most investigations were run by District 17 at Kirtland AFB, New Mexico. The 1948 green fireball investigations drew in a University of New Mexico meteoriticist; District 17 briefed Sandia Base, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory, the University of California Geophysics Institute, the Atomic Energy Commission and the Armed Forces Special Weapons Project in early 1949. On the recommendation of an Air Force Scientific Advisory Board member in April 1949, District 17 established an observation post on the crest of the Sandia Mountains northeast of Albuquerque where agents manned spectrographic photo surveillance equipment twenty-four hours a day. The results were collected under OSI Letter Number 85: Unconventional Aircraft-Special Inquiry, classified file designation 24-185.

Two items in that same account matter disproportionately. First: "In 1967, agents briefed a scientific group on Neutron Activity analysis and sent a piece of an alleged UFO to the FBI Crime Laboratory. The lab concluded that while the item was unusual, there was no evidence that it belonged to an alien craft." This is an official, on-the-record acknowledgement of AFOSI custody and forensic routing of purported UAP material, and it is the same workflow that runs today through Oak Ridge. Second: AFOSI declassified its UFO investigative files in late 1975 and sent them to the National Archives, and Kidwell writes that "The National Archives has been unable to locate any documentation among the Blue Book records that discuss the incident in Roswell." The service whose district office covered New Mexico transferred its New Mexico UFO files to NARA and none of them mention Roswell - which sits alongside the GAO's separate finding that Roswell Army Air Field's outgoing messages for 1946-1949 were destroyed without recorded authority.

Then there is Kirtland in 1980. On 9 August 1980 security personnel at the Manzano Weapons Storage Area adjacent to Kirtland reported a bright light descending in a restricted area, and a report was filed with AFOSI at Kirtland. The investigating agent was Special Agent Richard C. Doty. In the same period Doty became the primary AFOSI contact for Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque physicist and businessman who had been filming and intercepting signals around Kirtland and Manzano. Rather than being turned away, Bennewitz was fed. Doty has since publicly acknowledged participating in counterintelligence disinformation directed at the UFO research community, and both Doty and documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe state they met at Kirtland AFB in April 1983. Bennewitz's mental deterioration is the documented outcome.

The reason this matters to a board about a legacy program is not that Doty's stories were true. It is that they were false, deliberately, and produced under colour of federal counterintelligence authority at the base where the Air Force's New Mexico UFO files, its nuclear weapons storage and its special access program security responsibilities all converged. Disinformation is expensive and is not deployed to protect nothing. AFOSI's own charter tells you what it protects at Kirtland: special access programs and nuclear surety. Whether the thing being screened was a conventional black program, a nuclear security vulnerability, or the retrieval architecture itself is exactly the question - and AFOSI is the agency whose files would settle it.

AFOSI remains inside the current reporting architecture. The May 2023 Joint Staff GENADMIN reproduced in AARO's FY2024 annual report directs Combatant Commands and Services to report all UAP incidents, incursions and engagements to Joint Operations Centers, Service Watch Centers, and respective counterintelligence elements within 96 hours. For the Department of the Air Force, per AFMD 39 paragraph 3.3, that counterintelligence element is AFOSI and only AFOSI.

dossier.whatItIs: The Air Force Office of Special Investigations (AFOSI) is the Department of the Air Force's federal law enforcement and counterintelligence agency, established 1 August 1948 and operating as a Field Operating Agency under the Secretary of the Air Force Inspector General. Its first commander was Special Agent Joseph F. Carroll, a senior FBI official and assistant to Director J. Edgar Hoover, who in 1961 became the first Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency. AFOSI is currently chartered by Air Force Mission Directive 39, dated 12 February 2024.
dossier.whyImplicated: AFOSI sits on both sides of the concealment problem simultaneously, and its own charter says so. Under AFMD 39 paragraph 3.16 it "Executes independent special access program CI and LE investigations, operations, specialized investigative activities, compliance inspections, integrated technology protection, and program security responsibilities for all DAF special access programs, and non-DAF special access programs where the DAF has been assigned responsibility." That is the security envelope around Air Force black programs, held by one agency. Under paragraph 3.3 it is the Department's sole counterintelligence agency, and under 3.2 its investigations supersede any other Air Force entity's inquiry. Historically, AFOSI took over UFO investigation from Air Materiel Command shortly after its 1948 creation under the name Project Grudge, ran most of those investigations out of District 17 at Kirtland AFB in New Mexico - the district co-located with Sandia, Los Alamos and the Manzano weapons storage area - and in 1967 sent a piece of an alleged UFO to the FBI Crime Laboratory. And the single best-documented instance of a US counterintelligence element manufacturing UFO belief, the campaign run against Albuquerque physicist Paul Bennewitz in the late 1970s and 1980s, was run by an AFOSI special agent at Kirtland.
